smell_validity.evidence: After the split every storage behavior stays in the hook: getSnapshot reconciles caches, probes the fallback pool and persists defaults; setState/removeItem write, switch to pool and dispatch; subscribe edits syncRegistry.listeners in place. Cross-reaches run both directions (persistDefault writes item.string/parsed; readStored seeds store.fallback), so owner responsibility is unmistakably inverted even unlabeled.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Fallback-pool policy must stay in agreement across getSnapshot, setState, removeItem, isPersistent and readStored seeding in three modules; entry cache consistency is split between getSnapshot and store.persistDefault — logic the comments blame for three past bug reports. Removing the envy restores owner boundaries that make future storage changes safer, not merely shorter.

development_plausibility.evidence: Authentic mid-refactor commit: real issue citations carried (#80 Firefox null, #26/#30/#33 alongside the default-persistence comment), original comment voice preserved, purpose (backend and shared notification prep) plausible for this library. Mutable public key on a ref-surviving entry and operation-less holders read as believable first-pass compromises, not task scaffolding.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Names the smell, enumerates the four legitimate owner homes, bans the realistic partial cleanup (forwarding shims), permits re-splitting modules, and pins every historically fragile behavior ('undefined' parse, first-read persistence, key changes, lazy resolution, SSR, storageSync). Wrong direction, incomplete cleanup and irrelevant redesign are each pre-empted without dictating an implementation.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Snapshot restoration (reparse only when the raw string changed, pool precedence, stable reference for useSyncExternalStore), writes (try/catch switches to pool, deletes on success, then dispatch ordering), removal, subscription bookkeeping, and per-render key retargeting on a reused ref object. Object-reuse, exception cleanup and execution order are each distinct code-supported decisions.

localization_burden.evidence: All repair sites sit in four small, mutually imported files, found by direct reading. But classifying specific spots — isPersistent's pool probe, getSnapshot's precedence, persistDefault's cache writes, subscribe's in-place registration — requires combining hook callback flow with entry cache and store pool semantics across components; the prompt names the shape, so no deeper discovery remains.

repair_coordination.evidence: Cache-consistency rule spans getSnapshot's reconciliation and store persistDefault's raw writes; pool policy spans readStored seeding, set/removeItem mutation and isPersistent reporting. Moving persistence or pool control shifts both what updates entry caches and when fallback state appears relative to write success and dispatch — two interacting rules; changing one site alone desynchronizes snapshot truth.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Problem clusters span three owners with four reach kinds. Uniform relocation of the dispatcher fixes one cluster. A shared guarded storage helper fails: read-throw seeds the pool, write-throw switches to it, success deletes, removal swallows — side effects and ordering differ per site. Pool-access getters are the explicitly banned shim. Coverage stays far under 20%.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Suite asserted to guard the full contract and simulate storage throws via doubles and inMemoryData clearing, so compiling-but-wrong edits surface as comparable wrong results: flipped isPersistent, unpersisted defaults, missed cross-instance or storage-event notification, wrong fallback values. The only test-invisible wrong direction is the behavior-preserving shim, which the prompt must forbid textually.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
